_howto: Production Pay how-to guides. mode click = the user clicks the real button. optional = skipped when that part isn't on screen. Never reuse a step id.

guides.title: Set up farms and units
guides.blurb: Add your farms and their field units, with their size and GPS location.

steps.title: Production Settings
steps.text: Farms and units live here. Click it.

steps.title: Farms & Units
steps.text: Click Farms & Units.

steps.title: 1. The farm
steps.text: Type the farm's name, for example Highlands.

steps.title: 2. Its location
steps.text: The map pin button opens a map. Search for the place, click the farm on the map and set a radius in metres around it. The badge above then shows the location is set.

steps.title: 3. Add
steps.text: Adds the farm. It then appears in the list below and in the unit's farm list.

steps.title: 4. A unit on the farm
steps.text: Choose the farm the unit belongs to.

steps.title: 5. Name and size
steps.text: The block, orchard or field name, and its size in hectares.

steps.title: 6. Its location
steps.text: Set the unit's own spot and radius on the map, the same way as the farm.

steps.title: 7. Add
steps.text: Adds the unit. Tasks are then given for these farms and units.

steps.title: Your list
steps.text: Edit names and sizes in place, change a boundary with the map button, or deactivate what you no longer use.

guides.title: Create a team and add its members
guides.blurb: Create a production team, choose how its manager is paid, and add its members.

steps.title: Teams
steps.text: Teams live here. Click it.

steps.title: 1. Team name
steps.text: For example Harvest Team A.

steps.title: 2. Asset tags (optional)
steps.text: Type a tag and press Enter for each one, for example the tractor or trailer the team uses.

steps.title: 3. The manager's share
steps.text: For team work: neither ticked = the manager is paid for the full team quantity; Equal Share = the manager gets a worker's share; Average Only = the manager gets the workers' average.

steps.title: 4. Create Team
steps.text: Click Create Team (or skip it if you're only practising), then click Next.

steps.title: 5. Open the team
steps.text: Click the team's card to set it up.

steps.title: Team details
steps.text: Rename the team, change its tags or the manager's share, then Save Details.

steps.title: Add members
steps.text: Search by name or PIN, or filter by department. Tick people and click Add Selected.

steps.title: The team's manager
steps.text: Choose the manager and click Assign. The manager is paid at the manager rate.

steps.title: Audit History
steps.text: Everyone who joined or left the team, and when.

steps.title: Deactivate
steps.text: Deactivate a team you no longer use. Its history is kept, and you can reactivate it from Deactivated Teams.

guides.title: Add an activity and its rate
guides.blurb: Add what people are paid for, and keep its rates over time in the Pricing Ledger.

steps.title: Activities & Pricing
steps.text: Activities live here. Click it.

steps.title: Add Activity
steps.text: Click Add Activity.

steps.title: Activity Name
steps.text: What the work is, for example Apple Picking.

steps.title: Unit of Measure
steps.text: What it's counted in, for example bins, crates or trees. Quantities in Daily Production use this unit.

steps.title: Worker Rate
steps.text: What a worker earns per unit.

steps.title: Manager Rate (optional)
steps.text: What a team's manager earns per unit, if different.

steps.title: Save
steps.text: Saves the activity with these rates from today. Click Save (or Cancel if you're only practising), then Next.

steps.title: Pricing Ledger
steps.text: When a rate changes, don't edit the activity. Add the new rate in its Pricing Ledger, with the date it starts. Click it on an activity.

steps.title: New rates
steps.text: The new worker and manager rate.

steps.title: Effective Date
steps.text: The first day the new rate applies. Days before it keep the old rate, so past production is never re-priced.

steps.title: Log Price
steps.text: Adds the rate to the ledger. The list below shows every rate the activity has had.

guides.title: Create a task
guides.blurb: Give work to a team or phone user: activities and targets, where, how it's paid, evidence and dates.

steps.title: Tasks
steps.text: Tasks live here. Click it.

steps.title: Create Task
steps.text: Click Create Task.

steps.title: Task Name
steps.text: Required. Something the team will recognise, for example Morning Apple Harvest - Block 5.

steps.title: Asset tags and vehicles
steps.text: Optional. Type a tag and press Enter for equipment used on this task, and pick any vehicles that work on it.

steps.title: Farm and units
steps.text: Choose the farm (the search box above filters the list), then the units. Leave the units empty to cover the whole farm.

steps.title: Activities and targets
steps.text: Click Add Activity for each kind of work in this task, and give each one a target quantity. The target drives the task's progress bar.

steps.title: Evidence from the phone
steps.text: Whether a photo and a signature are optional, mandatory or switched off, and whether they're collected once at the end of the task or with every capture.

steps.title: Payment Method
steps.text:
Pay per Individual: each worker is paid for what they captured.
Pay per Team: the team's total is shared equally among the members who clocked in that day, and the manager is paid by the team's manager setting.

steps.title: Who does it
steps.text: Assign a team, a mobile user who captures for it, or both. The search boxes filter the lists.

steps.title: Start and estimated end
steps.text: The task shows on the phones and in Daily Production from the start date. The end date shows as its due date; it's marked overdue after that.

steps.title: Create Task
steps.text: Saves the task as Pending. Click Create Task (or Cancel if you're only practising).

steps.title: Then
steps.text: While it's Pending you can edit or delete it. Start makes it In Progress, and Complete closes it. Click a task any time to see what's been captured.

guides.title: Check and commit a day to payroll
guides.blurb: Load a team's day, check clockings and quantities, fix what's wrong, then commit it to payroll.

steps.title: Daily Production
steps.text: Each day is checked and committed here. Click it.

steps.title: 1. The day
steps.text: Choose the day to check.

steps.title: 2. The team
steps.text: Choose the team.

steps.title: 3. Load Grid
steps.text: Click Load Grid.

steps.title: 4. Clockings
steps.text: Each person's clock-in and clock-out from Time & Attendance. Someone with no clockings isn't paid a share of team work that day. Click the times to correct them; this overrides their clockings.

steps.title: 5. Quantities
steps.text: What each person captured on the phone, per activity. Type over a wrong quantity. On team-paid tasks the share is worked out for you and can't be typed over.

steps.title: 6. Times on each activity
steps.text: The start and end time spent on the activity. Use the copy button to give the same times to other people in one go.

steps.title: 7. Work that wasn't planned
steps.text: Add a column for an activity the team did that isn't on one of its tasks.

steps.title: 8. Hours and pay
steps.text: The last columns total each person's day: normal time, approved and potential overtime, Sunday/public holiday, then piece wage, time wage and the total. They update as you type.

steps.title: Filters
steps.text: Show only the people who did piecework, and sort PINs by their numbers only.

steps.title: 9. Save Draft
steps.text: Keeps your changes without making them final. You can come back and carry on.

steps.title: 10. Commit to Payroll
steps.text: Makes the day final: its records lock and count towards payroll. Only commit once everything is right.

steps.title: If something was wrong
steps.text:
Unlock reopens committed records so they can be changed. Revert Edits removes manual changes and puts back what the phones captured.

If the day falls in a locked payroll period (Employee Master › Payroll Periods), it can't be saved, committed, unlocked or reverted until that period is unlocked. You'll see who and which dates are affected.

guides.title: Run a production report
guides.blurb: Choose the dates, who to include and the report type, then view or export it.

steps.title: Production Reports
steps.text: Reports live here. Click it.

steps.title: 1. Dates
steps.text: Choose the start and end date.

steps.title: 2. Who
steps.text: A department, team or task, or particular employees from the Employees list. Leave them on All for everyone.

steps.title: 3. Report Type
steps.text:
• Daily Detailed: each person's production per day.
• Employee Daily Evidence: the photos captured with it.
• Employee Summary and Activity Summary: totals for the date range, per person or per activity.
• Job Costing (by employee), Job Costing Summary (a matrix of people and jobs) and Job Costing Wages (hours × hourly rate per day; the Global Hourly Rate applies here when it's switched on).
• Global Summary: everything combined.

steps.title: 4. Sort
steps.text: How the rows are ordered.

steps.title: 5. Generate Report
steps.text: Click Generate Report to see it.

steps.title: 6. Export to Excel
steps.text: Saves the report you've just generated as a spreadsheet.

guides.title: Check job costing
guides.blurb: Load a date range, find running and flagged jobs, and correct them.

steps.title: Job Costing
steps.text: Job costing lives here. Click it.

steps.title: 1. Dates
steps.text: Choose the start and end date.

steps.title: 2. Load Data
steps.text: Click Load Data.

steps.title: 3. What needs checking
steps.text:
Still Running and Flagged are the ones to look at.

A job is flagged when it ran over 14 hours or has no activity chosen. A job still running has no clock-out yet.

steps.title: 4. Flagged Only
steps.text: Show only the flagged jobs.

steps.title: 5. Open a person
steps.text: Click a person to see their jobs.

steps.title: 6. Correct a job
steps.text: Use Edit to choose the right unit or activity. A job with an activity is no longer flagged for having none.

steps.title: 7. Export
steps.text: Save the list to Excel if you need it elsewhere.
